candidates.why_underfollowed: It is usually classified as a trade-school or for-profit education name, not as a beneficiary of K-12-to-career pathway expansion or state workforce-training policy.

memory_update.text: LRN should remain the reference anchor for the K-12 virtual schooling and career-learning node because it directly discloses virtual/blended public-school and Career Learning exposure.

LINC is a viable underfollowed postsecondary-skills pathway candidate; later layers should test whether growth is driven by employer/state workforce demand or simply campus expansion and Title IV enrollment cycles.
FC is a small-cap, curriculum-adjacent school-execution supplier candidate through Leader in Me; verify Education Division materiality and public-school procurement exposure.
NNI is an indirect infrastructure/speculative-shadow candidate for education payments, servicing, and admin rails; it needs segment/customer proof before promotion beyond Layer 1.
Need a separate pass for private curriculum/assessment vendors and public acquirers/parents, because many obvious K-12 virtual-school suppliers are private or embedded inside diversified publishers.

node: K-12 virtual schooling, career learning, and postsecondary skills pathways
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the K-12 virtual-schooling and career-learning node found one direct reference leader and three underfollowed or second-order candidates. The direct validator is Stride, whose filings explicitly tie revenue to virtual/blended public schools, general education, and career learning. The underfollowed lane points to smaller or less-pure assets around postsecondary workforce training, school leadership/curriculum software, and education-finance/admin infrastructure. The key chokepoint to test in later layers is not generic edtech demand, but state authorization, school/customer contracting, program approvals, instructor availability, student services, and funding/payment rails.
